subject: POC scope, model recommendation, and evaluation milestones
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff + next steps (POC scope + model pick)

Hi Liam — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap and a proposed POC plan so we can lock timelines. Please flag anything I missed.

What we heard (prioritized):
- Primary success criteria: extraction accuracy for product-attribute pairs >= 90% F1 on the evaluation set (customer-labeled), and median generation relevance (human eval) >= 4.2/5 for freeform answers.
- Latency: median server-side response < 300 ms for short completion flows (<= 256 tokens).
- Throughput: baseline target 40 req/sec sustained for concurrent UI usage.
- Multilingual: English + Spanish + French must be supported; Spanish is the priority after English (10–15% of traffic).

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks):
1) Day 0–2: Kickoff, data handoff + access (sample prompts, eval set, schema).
2) Day 3–6: Baseline runs: evaluate two open model candidates on a 200-sample eval set + latency/cost profiling.
3) Day 7–12: Narrow to chosen model + fallback variant; run 1,000-sample eval and human relevance check; iterate prompts.
4) Day 13–14: Final results, recommendations, and next steps for rollout or Dedicated sizing.

Model recommendation (initial):
- Primary: Mistral-7B-Instruct (good cost/latency balance, strong instruction-following for extractions).
- Fallback / higher-quality variant: Llama-2-13B-chat (use for long-form answers and as a failover on quality-sensitive routes).
- On-prem / quantized fallback: Llama-2-13B-q4 (4-bit quantized) if you need Private deployment with reduced memory.

Why this mix: Mistral-7B gives us lower token cost and faster median latency for short responses; Llama-2-13B provides robustness on complex multi-turn or ambiguous prompts. We will include a routing rule during the POC so ~10% of traffic is sent to the higher-quality variant for comparison.

Ownership:
- Acme: Liam (product lead) — eval labels + prompt priorities + PO for procurement.
- Redwood: Naomi (sales lead) — timelines and commercial coordination; Ben (solutions eng) — infra/setup and benchmarks; Camila (ML ops) — eval harness and scoring.

Attachments: I attached the draft evaluation checklist and sample prompts (poc-eval-plan.xlsx, sample-prompts.txt) and a short SOW for procurement (redwood-poc-sow.pdf).

Next steps / asks:
- Liam: confirm sample eval set availability by Wed EOD (Jun 17).
- Procurement: approximate PO timing — do you need a vendor form filled?
- Ben/Camila: we'll do a quick infra sync tomorrow to confirm credentials and region (us-west).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the Day 0 kickoff.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Kickoff + next steps (technical notes and infra)

Quick tech note to prep for the Day 0 kickoff. High-level infra plan: 

- Hosted POC on Redwood API (us-west) for fastest time-to-value. We'll spin up two model endpoints: mistral-7b-instruct (primary) and llama-2-13b-chat (fallback).
- Autoscaling: set min instances = 1, max = 4 for mistral; fallback set to on-demand (manual scale) to control cost.
- KV caching: enable prefix caching for common prompt templates (should lower tail latency).
- Multilingual tokenization: both candidates support Spanish/French but we should add language-specific prompt templates for improved accuracy.

Benchmark plan for Day 3–6:
- 200-sample run: measure token-level latency, median throughput, average cost per 1k tokens.
- Human eval: Camila will run a blind relevance survey (3 raters) for the 200-sample set.

Risk notes:
- Llama-2-13B may exceed memory on smaller Dedicated nodes without quantization — for Dedicated sizing we should consider 80GB GPU targets or quantized variant.
- If Acme needs on-prem, we’ll prepare a quantization/packaging step (extra 2–3 days).

I’ll prepare the runbook and a minimal infra checklist before the kickoff. Naomi — I pushed a provisional calendar slot for tomorrow morning.

— Ben
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
